learning_objective: 🎯 Discover the vast oceans, their dynamic movements, and their crucial role in regulating climate and sustaining life on Earth!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Oceans cover about 71% of Earth's surface. They are bodies of saline (salty) water that are all interconnected. The major oceans are the Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Southern, and Arctic.
Waves are created by wind pushing on the surface. Ocean Currents are like massive rivers flowing steadily within the ocean, carrying warm or cold water across the globe.
Tides are the rhythmic rise and fall of ocean water twice a day. They are caused primarily by the strong gravitational pull of the Moon and the Sun on Earth's water.
Oceans are teeming with life, from microscopic plankton to giant blue whales. Areas where warm and cold currents meet (like Newfoundland) are the world's best fishing grounds.
Oceans absorb massive amounts of solar heat and distribute it around the world. Without ocean currents, the equator would be boiling hot, and the poles would be freezing solid.

fun_activity.title: 🧂 The Floating Egg
fun_activity.instructions: Place an egg in a glass of tap water; it will sink. Now stir 4-5 spoons of salt into the water and try again. The egg floats! This shows how ocean 'salinity' increases the density and buoyancy of water.

exam_tips: 📌 Clearly differentiate between Waves (surface wind), Tides (moon's gravity), and Currents (temperature/salinity differences).
📌 Know the difference between Spring Tides (highest tides during full/new moon) and Neap Tides (lower tides during quarter moons).
📌 Explain how warm ocean currents bring rain to coastal areas, while cold currents often create deserts on the western coasts of continents.
quick_recap: ⭐ The Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest ocean on Earth.
⭐ Salinity is the amount of salt dissolved in water; the Dead Sea has incredibly high salinity.
⭐ Tsunamis are giant waves caused by underwater earthquakes or volcanoes, NOT by the wind.
